question: What is the primary driver of inherited degenerative diseases?

options.A: Genetic mutations passed down through families
options.B: Vitamin deficiencies acquired during early childhood
options.C: Acute bacterial infections of the central nervous system

explanation: Inherited degenerative diseases stem from abnormal genetic blueprints passed from parents to offspring, leading to progressive cell breakdown. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h1)

question: Why do mental health challenges occur alongside physical decline in neurodegenerative conditions?

options.A: Patients choose to neglect their emotional well-being
options.B: Brain cell breakdown directly alters neurotransmitter systems
options.C: Hospital environments trigger sudden psychological distress
options.D: Standard medications cause permanent cognitive damage

explanation: Structural degradation in the brain disrupts chemical messengers responsible for mood and cognition. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h1)

question: A patient with Huntington's disease develops sudden unprovoked paranoia. This symptom is classified as what?
explanation: Paranoid beliefs and hallucinations fall under the category of psychotic symptoms resulting from brain degeneration. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h2)

question: Depression in inherited degenerative diseases is caused by which factor?

options.A: A temporary reaction to changing hospital diets
options.B: Both neurochemical disruption and the emotional weight of loss
options.C: Exclusively a lack of proper sleep schedules in the ward
options.D: Strictly a side effect of routine physical therapy

explanation: Chemical changes in the brain combine with the psychological grief of losing physical and mental abilities to cause depression. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h2)

question: Why is collateral history from family members important during a mental health assessment?

options.A: Patients are unable to speak at any stage of the disease
options.B: Hospital policy mandates family participation in medication administration
options.C: Family members hold the most accurate picture of baseline behaviour
options.D: Relatives are legally required to sign all nursing care plans

explanation: Relatives notice subtle personality and behavioural shifts that occur long before formal clinical assessments take place. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h3)

question: A nurse notices a patient with a degenerative brain disease is increasingly apathetic and withdrawn. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Document the observation and compare it against previous baseline assessments
options.B: Discharge the patient immediately to reduce ward workload
options.C: Scold the patient for refusing to participate in daily ward activities
options.D: Administer a high dose of emergency sedatives without an order

explanation: Tracking changes against a known baseline helps determine the progression of psychiatric manifestations. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h3)

question: Which non-pharmacological strategy helps minimize anxiety in patients with neurodegenerative conditions?

options.A: Maintaining consistent daily schedules and structured routines
options.B: Rotating nursing staff every hour to create novelty
options.C: Constantly changing the patient's room to stimulate the brain
options.D: Isolating the patient completely from all human contact

explanation: Predictable daily routines reduce the confusion and anxiety common in degenerative brain diseases. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h4)

question: Why must nurses exercise caution when administering psychotropic medications to patients with neurodegenerative diseases?

options.A: Drugs in this class are completely ineffective in neurological cases
options.B: These medications cure the underlying genetic mutation instantly
options.C: Standard dosages always cause immediate permanent memory loss
options.D: Patients can have heightened sensitivity and severe motor side effects

explanation: Damaged neurological pathways make these patients far more vulnerable to adverse drug reactions, particularly extrapyramidal symptoms. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h4)

question: What term describes the grief family members feel while watching a loved one slowly decline?
explanation: Anticipatory grief occurs when people mourn an impending loss long before the actual death takes place, common in progressive illnesses. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h5)

question: How do nursing interventions help reduce caregiver burnout in chronic degenerative diseases?

options.A: Encouraging relatives to isolate themselves to avoid stress
options.B: Instructing families to handle all care tasks without outside help
options.C: Taking over financial responsibilities for the entire household
options.D: Connecting families with support groups and respite care services

explanation: Respite care and support groups give exhausted caregivers essential breaks and emotional backing. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h5)

question: What document helps guide medical decisions when a patient loses decision-making capacity?
explanation: An advance directive outlines a patient's preferences for medical care before they lose the ability to make decisions. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h6)

question: Why is ethical decision-making particularly challenging in advanced neurodegenerative diseases?

options.A: Palliative care eliminates all need for ethical discussions
options.B: Patients lose cognitive capacity, requiring others to interpret their best interests
options.C: Families always agree unanimously on every treatment option
options.D: Medical staff have legal ownership over the patient's personal assets

explanation: When patients cannot speak for themselves, surrogates and nurses must navigate difficult choices about comfort and life-prolonging treatments. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h6)
